sections.name: Versus scoring and distance
sections.card:
Summary: In Left 4 Dead 2 versus, only the team on the survivor side scores, and most of its points come from distance. Each survivor is credited with the furthest spot they get to, so one who turns back and dies keeps the ground already covered.
Tips: A survivor who is alive when the chapter ends is worth 25 more points to the team, unless they die in the safe room before its door shuts. Health and carried items no longer change the score, and reviving a dead survivor with a defibrillator costs 25 points.
Tips: A tie where every survivor reached the safe room on both sides is settled by damage: the team whose infected players did more gets 25 bonus points. That tiebreaker does not apply when someone died, even if the scores are equal. Both sides are told whenever the survivors pass another 25% of the distance.
Tips: The wiki's Tactics page tells survivors to focus on making progress rather than tracking down a Hunter, and says this matters most in versus. Its Realism Versus page adds that moving slowly and carefully can sometimes beat racing ahead when you are going for team points.

sections.name: Versus special infected spawn order and mixes
sections.card:
Summary: When a versus infected player's wait to respawn is over, the AI Director assigns which special infected they become.
Tips: In Left 4 Dead 2 versus, the four infected players nearly always get four different specials. The Director seldom deals out four pinners (Smoker, Charger, Hunter, Jockey), which keeps the team from pinning all four survivors in one move; Boomer and Spitter support instead of pinning.
Tips: The Tank is a random extra, at most one per level, and your chance of getting him rises with your score. After the sides swap, the other team usually starts with the same specials in the same places and order.
Tips: With fewer than three infected players, bots fill the empty slots and the Director may spawn two of the same type, or all the bot specials at once. With four infected players the respawn wait can reach 30 seconds, about 20 on average.

sections.name: Versus ghost mode and spawning
sections.card:
Summary: When the respawn timer runs out, a versus infected player becomes a ghost: the screen takes on a blue tint, and they choose where to appear. Survivors cannot see a ghost; its teammates see it outlined in blue.
Tips: You can appear on any clear ground at a middling distance from the survivors (not right beside them and not far off), out of their view and outside a restricted zone. The starting safe room counts as restricted until the survivors have left it.
Tips: A ghost can slip through doors, smashable objects and certain barricades, and nobody can damage it. Falling into a zone that kills on contact still ends it, and the respawn timer starts over just as it would after a normal death.
Tips: An infected player who falls well behind the survivors is offered a jump up to the group's position, which puts them in spawn mode there. Survivors deny a spot by watching it or standing near it, and a sudden dash that puts an important spot in view before the infected player there can react and spawn can wreck an ambush, though it is risky.

sections.name: Using the Witch as the infected team
sections.card:
Summary: In versus nobody can be the Witch, yet she is a useful trap: a single hit from her incapacitates a survivor on any difficulty, so the infected team can work her into its plans and send survivors toward her.
Tips: A Smoker can pull a survivor over to the Witch, and a Jockey can steer one toward her. A Spitter can protect her by spitting acid close to her; survivors hurrying out of the puddles may bump into her or end up next to her.
Tips: A Hunter or Boomer crouching in front of her blocks the survivors' view of her. If a Boomer dies while the survivors are fairly near her, the burst startles her and she goes after the one who killed it. In versus, a non-Tank infected player can also claw her once on spotting a survivor, which leaves her nearly enraged.
Tips: Skilled Hunters tend to wait, crouched and out of view, near the Witch; when a survivor rushes in to hit her, they leap on that survivor just before he can shoot. If a Hunter pounces on a survivor the Witch has already downed and is attacking, the Hunter takes no damage and the survivor dies twice as quickly. The infected see a calm Witch outlined in white, and the outline shifts toward red as she gets closer to being startled.

sections.name: Answering combined special attacks in versus
sections.card:
Summary: How versus survivors answer the infected team's bile and the grabs that follow: spread out enough that one burst cannot catch everyone, hold fire while blinded, stay close together, and break a grab quickly.
Tips: Do not stand too close together when a Boomer is around, so a single burst of bile cannot cover all four survivors. If he gets near, shove him back and retreat before firing, and only shoot once he is well clear of you and your teammates.
Tips: While you are covered in bile you cannot see, so shooting is likely to hit a teammate; shove instead and head for the nearest corner you can defend. The others should stay near the biled survivor, and a thrown pipe bomb can distract the horde.
Tips: A survivor who is alone and far from the group is an easy target for a Smoker, so keep close together when you hear one. A grabbed survivor has only a few seconds to shoot their way free.

sections.name: Charger ledge charges in versus
sections.card:
Summary: A Charger that sweeps survivors over a high drop can incapacitate or kill them, and the wiki calls his charge deadly near cliffs and ledges.
Tips: As the Charger, ambush instead of charging from far off, because a long run gives survivors time to react and dodge. You can start a charge from a raised spot without stopping first. A survivor clipped sideways beside a high drop may be left hanging and incapacitated, and one sent far enough past the edge may plunge to their death.
Tips: Survivors should not jump away from an oncoming Charger, since even a small drop in height can cause heavy fall damage or sudden death. Bots never attempt to avoid a charge, so keep them well away from him. Melee shoves have no effect, as he is immune to them; only explosives stumble him, and the grenade launcher is the one explosive that does not.

sections.name: Surviving Hunters and Jockeys
sections.card:
Summary: In versus, when a Hunter pins someone or a Jockey jumps on one, survivors standing nearby are thrown back, and in some places that leaves them dangling from a ledge. Stay a little apart, just far enough that the knockback does not reach your teammates.
Tips: Stay near at least one teammate. A crouching Hunter gives off a telltale growl just before he leaps; when you hear it, warn the other survivors. Hunters in versus, and on harder difficulties, tend to claw rather than leap, so a survivor whose health meter falls oddly fast is probably being attacked by one close by.
Tips: Against a Jockey, a melee shove knocks him off and stuns him, which gives you time to shoot. Moving constantly makes you harder to land on. If one is already riding you, steer against the direction he is pulling; that leaves you moving very slowly and gives teammates time to knock him off. When hazards like fire are close, deal with the Jockeys first.

sections.name: Surviving Smokers and Spitters
sections.card:
Summary: In versus a Smoker hurts his victim while pulling them along. A Spitter has little health, so any weapon can drop her in a handful of shots.
Tips: A Smoker usually attacks from behind you or from higher ground, though a few appear ahead of you. A grabbed teammate can be freed by killing the Smoker, shoving him, or breaking the tongue; a cut tongue regrows slowly and can strike again after about 15 seconds.
Tips: At long range, either a Hunting Rifle or a Sniper Rifle deals with a Spitter easily. When she dies she leaves a puddle of acid, a small one; hold back until it has gone, since neither detouring around it nor jumping over it works.
Tips: In a tight hallway, a versus Spitter that cannot hit survivors directly will spit across their route. They either push through the acid and get hurt, or hold back until it is gone, and holding back gives the Spitter's teammates time to respawn.

sections.name: Surviving the Tank
sections.card:
Summary: A versus Tank starts with 6000 health. As soon as the survivors walk into the area the Director picked for him, an infected player takes him over, and he is aggressive from the first moment.
Tips: Fire does more good than explosives: setting him alight with a Molotov or gas can keeps hurting him over time, though in versus burning no longer slows him down.
Tips: Stay away from the Tank whenever you can, and never let him trap you in a corner, since there is nowhere to go and you will probably be taken down.
Tips: When he is beating on a downed teammate, a survivor who shoves him or strikes him from behind can draw his attention away; shooting him does not do that. Any melee weapon deals 500 damage per swing, and explosives deal about 750.

sections.name: Infected team combinations
sections.card:
Summary: Coordinating their attacks is the most important thing for the infected side, according to the wiki: a Hunter pouncing alone is shot down before he does much harm, and a Smoker's catch gets freed with little trouble.
Tips: The Boomer should lead off, covering as many survivors in bile as possible. The Hunters then spring out of their hiding places and the Smoker pulls one survivor away. Should the bile land on a single survivor, go for the other three, who are clean, with pounces and the Smoker.
Tips: A Smoker that drags someone through a horde leaves a gap, and a Charger can use that gap to frighten off the survivors rushing to help. A Spitter should follow another special and spit on a survivor it has just pinned, particularly a Charger's or Hunter's. A Charger also does well to attack right after bile lands, picking survivors with no bile on them.
Tips: As a rule, the Boomer belongs out in front of the survivors, where he can lie in wait, and the Smoker behind them, where he can drag someone back; Hunters stay close to one of the two and exploit the confusion they cause. Hunters also do much better with something in front of them, such as the horde, a Charger or a Tank.

sections.name: Dead Center versus ambush spots
sections.card:
Summary: Charger ambush spots for the infected team on the first three chapters of Dead Center, The Hotel, The Streets and The Mall. Chargers do best on survivors squeezed into a narrow spot, lined up or bunched together.
Tips: The Hotel: charge a survivor standing beside a window with no railing on its ledge and they fall to their death. Try to pin someone in the fire lying between the lobby and the kitchen; it hurts far more than usual, and teammates reviving the downed survivor take heavy damage from it too.
Tips: The Streets: haul one survivor a long way from his teammates. The path leading up to the gun store is a long straight run, with little space for survivors to dodge. When they are on the ladder up the dumpster, climb up yourself and charge; this normally knocks every one of them back.
Tips: The Mall: take survivors over the edge of the upper floors. On an escalator, wait until all of them are riding it, then drive through the whole line the instant the front one reaches the far end; those sent flying may take fall damage.

sections.name: Dark Carnival versus ambush spots
sections.card:
Summary: Charger ambush spots for the infected team on the first four chapters of Dark Carnival: The Highway, The Fairgrounds, The Coaster and The Barns.
Tips: The Highway: in the motel, grab a survivor on the upper walkway and pull them off it, which delays and hurts them. Charge whoever is at the back just before the group leaps down the slope toward the swamp, and the victim is stranded and eventually dies. Toward the finish of the level you can also drive a survivor right back down that slope.
Tips: The Fairgrounds: once the survivors have climbed the building past Kiddie Land, a ramp sits behind the ladder, and you can charge them down it back toward Kiddie Land, which costs them a large amount of time or one of their team.
Tips: The Coaster: just as the survivors step out of the safe room by the Tunnel of Love and climb the stairs, come at them from the far side of the staircase and smash the lot of them against the wall. A variation is to spawn inside the safe room and charge toward the tunnel from the other direction, because the survivors are expecting a charge to come out of the tunnel.
Tips: The Barns: rooftops make a great spot to send survivors over the side. Survivors often line up in the long alley after the Crescendo Event, and concealing yourself in a crowd of common infected helps with that.

sections.name: Swamp Fever versus ambush spots
sections.card:
Summary: Charger ambush spots for the infected team on the first three chapters of Swamp Fever: Plank Country, The Swamp and Shanty Town.
Tips: Plank Country: when the survivors stand on the dock ahead of the Crescendo Event, seize one or, better still, send one tumbling into deep water; the one you grabbed and any you struck die at once. The same trick works when they step off the ferry on the far side of the map: wait behind a tree, then charge one of them off the dock. On the walkways, getting them to drop into the swamp slows them down a lot.
Tips: The Swamp: dunking survivors in the water pays off, since their whole team is slowed.
Tips: Shanty Town: you are not slowed by the water as the survivors are, so go after a survivor who is on their own. There are also a few cramped places to dash in and strike with a melee attack.

sections.name: Holding out in Survival mode
sections.card:
Summary: Survival is a mode in both Left 4 Dead games: wave after wave of infected keeps coming until every survivor is dead or incapacitated. It cannot be won; the aim is to last as long as possible and set records.
Tips: Before you start the horde, gather as many supplies as you can and settle on the best spot. Set up the special ammo, and put gas cans or propane tanks somewhere secure, so the team can grab them quickly in a Tank attack when no Molotovs are in hand.
Tips: To choose where to hold out, check the ammo and supplies nearby, the entrances, escape routes, high ground and how far you can see. Aim for just one or two ways in, so that two survivors can cover each of them.
Tips: The wiki's Survival tips give steady times for Tanks and hordes within the first 12 minutes: the first Tank at 0:40, and two together at both 5:30 and 11:30. New common-infected hordes stop for roughly 3:50 to 4:25, 9:00 to 9:35 and 12:00 to 12:30; only special infected can appear then, which makes those windows good for healing or an ammo run.

sections.name: Realism Versus
sections.card:
Summary: Realism Versus is ordinary versus with the same scoring, but the survivor side plays under Realism rules, which make common infected tougher and let a Witch kill with a single hit.
Tips: As a survivor, never go off alone: if you are in trouble away from the group, your teammates will probably not get to you in time. A Hunter's growl and a Smoker's cough are the sounds to catch; call them out when you hear them. Talk through a microphone rather than typing, since typing leaves you unable to defend yourself. Resist the pull of the top-tier special weapons such as the Grenade Launcher or M60 when you can; smart infected will sit on those spots and ambush whoever turns up.
Tips: Playing the infected, a survivor on their own is an easy kill. Camp spots where tier 2 weapons lie or healing supplies can be plainly seen, since survivors very often run to them. Infected hit harder in this mode, so even a few hits from a Charger can badly hurt the team. A Jockey can put any survivor down, whatever their health, because teammates first have to find the victim before they can shove him off.
Tips: Infected players still see survivor auras as usual, except that the Tank cannot see the red auras on cars and other objects he could throw at survivors. Realism Versus later lost every defibrillator to a patch, along with every first aid kit except the starting kits survivors are given at the beginning of a map.
